text:
Alex: quick heads-up — ran a microburst stability sweep across H100 / A100 / L40S (seqs=128,512,2048; bs=1,8,32). saw intermittent tail spikes on H100 at seq=2048, bs=8. looks like the kernel selector is oscillating between flashv2 and paged_fuse during short bursts.

Maria: can you paste the perf numbers? short table will do.

Alex: sure — summarized (tokens/s | median latency | p95 latency):
H100  seq=2048 bs=8: 45k tps | 12ms median | 240ms p95 (spikes)
A100  seq=2048 bs=8: 38k tps | 15ms median | 28ms p95
L40S  seq=2048 bs=8: 41k tps | 14ms median | 32ms p95
H100 seq=512 bs=8: 120k tps | 4ms median | 8ms p95
(only H100 shows the huge p95 inflation at long seqs)

Zheng: what was the bench command? can we repro locally?

Alex: command I ran:
```
./run_attn_bench --gpu H100 --model=gpt2-xl --seq=2048 --batch=8 --iters=400 --collect-trace=sel_trace.json
```

Alex: attaching small selector trace excerpt (timestamped lines):
```
[00:01:23.100] candidates: flashv2 score=0.72 mem_est=6.4GB pref=latency
[00:01:23.100] candidates: paged_fuse score=0.71 mem_est=6.2GB pref=throughput
[00:01:23.100] select -> flashv2
[00:01:23.220] exec_time flashv2=9.5ms kv_hits=0.98
[00:01:23.221] select -> paged_fuse  <-- immediate flip next request
[00:01:23.340] exec_time paged_fuse=46ms kv_hits=0.65  <-- big slowdown
[00:01:23.341] select -> flashv2  <-- flip back
```

Maria: interesting — the flip back/forth aligns with kv_hits changing. when kv hit ratio drops, paged_fuse appears to be picked and stalls. why would paged_fuse be chosen when its score is marginally lower?

Ryan: our selector scoring includes mem margin + expected throughput + a small randomness term. small jitter in mem_est or kv state can cause marginal ties to flip. for microbursts we should enforce hysteresis (require >0.05 score delta to switch) or lock selection for N requests.

Zheng: +1 for hysteresis. also, the paged_fuse implementation does a slightly heavier kernel launch pattern when KV cache is colder — that could amplify latency. can we reproduce with a scripted kv-hit transition?

Alex: I ran a quick isolate: start warm (kv_hits~0.99) for 50 iters, then feed many short prompts to flush some cache -> kv_hits drops to ~0.6 and selector flips. snippet:
```
iter 1-50: kv_hits=0.99, flashv2 selected, lat=9-13ms
iter 51-70: kv_hits=0.62, paged_fuse selected, lat=40-80ms
iter 71-90: kv_hits=0.95, flashv2 selected, lat back to 10-15ms
```

Maria: ok — that shows causality. action items?

Ryan: proposal: (1) add hysteresis to selector: require delta >= 0.06 OR hold selection for min_stable=3 requests, (2) add kv_hit_ratio as an explicit input to scoring (so we don't treat it as noise), (3) run A/B canary on a single H100 pool.

Zheng: also add a guard: if p95 latency for chosen kernel jumps >3x over last N runs, fallback immediately to the other kernel but mark as transient and avoid flip-flopping for M seconds.

Alex: I'll prepare a small patch for hysteresis + kv_hint and a repro harness that toggles kv hit ratio. will push to branch microburst-fix and run canary.

ci-bot: auto-bench finished for artifacts/2505801234 — flamegraphs + traces uploaded (trace.html, sel_trace.json).

Maria: thanks. assign to Ryan/Zheng for review, Alex for patch and run. let's target a canary on a 3-node H100 pool tomorrow. :thumbsup:
